Here, we developed GrB@A-nChap, a cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)-inspired nanotherapeutic that chaperones granzyme B (GrB) into the tumor cell cytosol to supplement deficient cytotoxic effector activity in "cold" tumors. Mechanistically, GrB@A-nChap protects GrB under physiological conditions, undergoes partial protonation in the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment to enhance tumor cell uptake, and further responds to lysosomal acidity to promote acidity-dependent lysosomal escape and cytosolic GrB release. Cytosolic GrB then induces mitochondrial dysfunction, caspase-3 activation, and GSDME cleavage, thereby triggering an apoptosis-pyroptosis cascade. This cell death process is accompanied by ICD-associated molecular signals and enhanced dendritic cell maturation. In vivo, GrB@A-nChap treatment was associated with increased intratumoral immune cell infiltration and local immune modulation and enhanced the therapeutic response to αPD-1 treatment. This work establishes a CTLinspired nanotherapeutic that enables cytosolic GrB delivery and provides cell independent GrB-mediated tumor cell killing, offering a potential strategy for complementing existing treatments for cold tumors.© 2026 The Authors. Nucleic acidsMol Ther Nucleic AcidsMessenger RNA vaccines and beyond: Molecular design, delivery platforms, and emerging therapeutic applications.10314010314010314010.1016/j.omtn.2026.103140Messenger RNA (mRNA) medicine has progressed from a conceptual nucleic acid modality to a clinically validated platform for transient protein expression, with SARS-CoV-2 vaccines providing population-scale proof of maturity. This review synthesizes the molecular and translational principles underlying this transition, emphasizing two determinants of mRNA performance: transcript engineering and delivery formulation. Transcript engineering integrates cap structure, untranslated regions, coding-sequence optimization, nucleoside chemistry, and poly(A) design, whereas formulation controls encapsulation, tissue tropism, cytosolic release, stability, and route-dependent biodistribution. We examine how this platform logic extends beyond vaccination to protein replacement, lung-directed gene complementation, regenerative signaling, in vivo antibody production, local tumor immunomodulation, genome editing, and transient ex vivo cell engineering. We also compare conventional mRNA, self-amplifying RNA, and circular RNA as complementary architectures with distinct dose requirements, expression durability, immunogenicity, and manufacturability. Across preventive and therapeutic settings, translation is constrained by extrahepatic delivery specificity, productive endosomal escape, innate and carrier-driven immune responses during repeat dosing, and scalable manufacturing with robust analytical quality control. 2405-5808482026DecBiochemistry and biophysics reportsBiochem Biophys RepEngineered exosomes for breast cancer immunotherapy: Emerging strategies and translational potential.10282210282210282210.1016/j.bbrep.2026.102822Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality in women worldwide, despite significant advances in early detection and conventional therapies. Immunotherapy has emerged as a promising strategy to harness the body's immune system to combat tumors. However, limitations such as immune escape mechanisms and inefficient drug delivery continue to challenge its effectiveness. In recent years, engineered exosomes, cell-derived nanoscale vesicles, have gained attention as innovative carriers for cancer immunotherapy due to their natural biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, and inherent targeting capabilities. This review highlights recent advancements in the design and functionalization of exosomes for breast cancer immunotherapy, including the loading of immune-stimulating molecules, genetic cargos, and surface modifications to enhance tumor specificity. We also discuss their advantages over conventional nanocarriers, immunological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and challenges related to clinical translation. Grounded in the cancer immunoediting theory of "elimination-equilibrium-escape," this review systematically reconstructs the spatiotemporal continuum of OLK transitioning toward malignant conversion. We comprehensively dissect the localized immunosuppressive network centered on T cell exhaustion, Natural killer cell inactivation, M2 macrophage polarization, antigen-presenting cell defects, and the dual roles of fibroblasts, elucidating the interactive mechanisms that drive mucosal barrier collapse and immune escape. Accordingly, this paper focuses on the translational pathways of leveraging multimodal deep learning algorithms and big data oncology to integrate heterogeneous omics data, thereby constructing chairside precision decision-making systems. 1878-17051902026Dec01International immunopharmacologyInt ImmunopharmacolTumor-derived acetylcholine promotes immune evasion in hepatocellular carcinoma by protecting regulatory T cells from ferroptosis.11750111750110.1016/j.intimp.2026.117501S1567-5769(26)01349-4Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by immune suppression and limited durability of systemic therapy, yet how tumor metabolic remodeling supports regulatory T-cell (Treg) persistence remains unclear. Here, we identify a cholinergic immune-evasion pathway that links acetylcholine (ACh) accumulation to Treg ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Sorafenib-resistant patient-derived xenografts showed enhanced Treg-associated signatures together with enrichment of ferroptosis- and cholinergic signaling-related pathways. Clinical HCC tissues exhibited cholinergic remodeling, characterized by reduced BCHE, increased CHKA, elevated intratumoral ACh, increased Treg infiltration, and poor patient survival. Functionally, exogenous ACh and HCC cell-conditioned media protected MT-2 Treg-like cells from erastin-induced ferroptosis by reducing Fe2+ accumulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, lipid peroxidation and mitochondrial injury while restoring antioxidant capacity. ChAT knockdown in HCC cells weakened this protection, whereas ACh supplementation restored it. Mechanistically, ACh acted through α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR) to activate signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) phosphorylation and nuclear translocation. STAT3 directly bound the ubiquitin-specific peptidase 11 (USP11) promoter and induced USP11 transcription. USP11 interacted with ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1) and stabilized FSP1 by suppressing ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation, thereby limiting ferroptosis and reinforcing an immunosuppressive marker profile. Inhibition of STAT3, USP11 or FSP1 abolished the ferroptosis-protective effect of ACh. In vivo, targeting the Ach-Treg ferroptosis pathway restrained HCC growth, reduced intratumoral Treg accumulation, and enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy. Collectively, these findings identify a tumor-derived cholinergic mechanism that promotes Treg ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC, and highlight this process as a potential therapeutic vulnerability for combination immunotherapy.Copyright © 2026.
